sections.h2: What is the New Braunfels property tax rate?
sections.html:
The City of New Braunfels lists a 2025 total rate of $0.408936 per $100 of valuation. Of that, $0.193888 pays debt service and the remaining $0.215048 funds operations and maintenance in the General Fund.

The city is only one line on a New Braunfels bill. The school district, Comal County and any special districts add their own rates, and the Comal Appraisal District can tell you which units apply to your address. For the newest city rate after 2025, read the city's Tax Information page, which is where the figures above come from.

sections.h2: Who appraises and collects tax in New Braunfels?
sections.html:
The Comal Appraisal District sets values, and the city says it partners with the Comal County Tax Assessor-Collector to collect its property tax. The appraisal district is at 900 S. Seguin Ave., New Braunfels, TX 78130, open Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., with phone numbers 830-625-8597 and 830-625-8598.

Texas has no state property tax. The appraisal district values each parcel as of January 1, and the tax assessor-collector mails bills around October 1, according to the Comptroller. If part of your address sits in Guadalupe County, ask the Guadalupe County tax office which bill applies to you.

  • Appraisal and exemptions: Comal Appraisal District, 830-625-8597.
  • Paying the bill: the Comal County Tax Assessor-Collector, linked from the city's tax page.
  • City tax and rental tax questions: the city's main line, 830-221-4000, or the treasury office at 830-221-4369 for hotel tax.

sections.h2: When is New Braunfels property tax due?
sections.html:
Tax is due on receipt of the bill and counts as paid on time through January 31, since the Comptroller says unpaid taxes become delinquent on February 1. The bill usually arrives in October.

The first day of delinquency brings a 6 percent penalty and 1 percent interest. Penalty grows 1 percent a month until July 1, when it reaches 12 percent, and interest runs 1 percent per month with no maximum. A private attorney hired by a taxing unit can add up to 20 percent more.

  • Owners who are 65 or older, or disabled, may split the bill into four installments.
  • Some collectors allow payment plans of up to 36 months, and a plan is required only for a residence homestead.
  • A penalty waiver must be requested in writing before the 181st day after delinquency.

When a house sells, remember that the tax lien attaches every January 1 and that the owner on that date is liable for the year, even after the deed changes hands.

sections.h2: Which exemptions can New Braunfels homeowners claim?
sections.html:
The state requires school districts to exempt $140,000 of a residence homestead's value, and owners 65 or older or disabled get $60,000 more at the school level. Cities and counties may add their own, and the Comal Appraisal District keeps the current schedule for every New Braunfels taxing unit, so ask it for the city and county amounts.

The district's exemptions page covers these categories:

  • Residence homestead, over-65, disabled person, and the surviving spouses of owners who held those exemptions.
  • Disabled veteran exemptions, including a 100 percent disabled veteran's homestead.
  • Heir property, the 11.35 disaster exemption, and tax deferral for owners 65 or older or disabled.
  • Notes on selling or buying a home with an existing homestead exemption, and on losing the homestead cap.

Applications use Form 50-114. Most are due by April 30, and a buyer who closes after January 1 may claim the exemption for the rest of that year if the seller did not have one. A homestead also carries a cap that limits yearly increases in appraised value to 10 percent, beginning the year after it is first granted.

sections.h2: How do I protest a New Braunfels appraisal?
sections.html:
Write to the appraisal review board by May 15, or by the 30th day after the notice reaches you if that is later. Notices for homesteads go out about April 1.

The Comal Appraisal District also runs a taxpayer liaison officer, reachable at 830-626-4874. If the board does not settle it, an owner can take the dispute to district court or binding arbitration, and to the State Office of Administrative Hearings when the board's value is above $1,000,000. Pay the undisputed tax before February 1 while you appeal so penalties do not stack.

sections.h2: Does New Braunfels allow short-term rentals?
sections.html:
A short-term rental is a one- or two-family home rented for stays under 30 days, and the city's rules are strict. The city page says short-term rentals are not allowed in any residential zoning district, need a special use permit in most non-residential districts, and are barred from the floodway.

This matters when you sell a house advertised as a rental. The page lists a permit that requires proof of ownership, a site plan, a floor plan, commercial liability insurance of at least $500,000 per occurrence, and a $206 fee covering the permit and annual fire inspection. Renewal runs $128, and an annual life safety inspection by the Fire Marshal's Office is required.

Owners of an ordinary single-family house face none of those permit steps, but the same zoning check helps a buyer who plans to rent the place out. Ask the planning office at 830-221-4050 whether a specific address can be registered before you promise that use in a contract.

Short-term rentals owe a 7 percent hotel occupancy tax to the city on top of the state's 6 percent, due on the 20th of each month, with late fees starting at $50. A buyer should ask for the permit history and any unpaid hotel tax before closing, and a listing cannot be posted until the unit is permitted.

sections.h2: What do the Census numbers say about New Braunfels?
sections.html:
New Braunfels added residents quickly: the Census Bureau estimated 122,492 residents on July 1, 2025, against 90,403 in the 2020 census and 57,740 in 2010. That is a 35.5 percent gain since the 2020 base.

For 2020 through 2024, the owner-occupied rate was 65.3 percent and the median home value was $339,400. Median owner costs came to $2,088 a month with a mortgage and $745 without, median gross rent was $1,654, and median household income was $86,021. The city has 40,991 households on 45.18 square miles of land, with 14.9 percent of residents aged 65 or older. Mean travel time to work was 27.1 minutes.

On the sales tax side, the city's tax page puts the total sales and use tax at 8.25 percent, of which the city receives 1.5 percent.

faqs.q: What is the New Braunfels city tax rate for 2025?
faqs.a: It is $0.408936 per $100 of valuation, according to the City of New Braunfels. Debt service accounts for $0.193888 and operations for $0.215048.

faqs.q: Who collects property tax for New Braunfels?
faqs.a: The Comal County Tax Assessor-Collector collects the city's property tax under a partnership the city describes on its tax page. The Comal Appraisal District, at 900 S. Seguin Ave., handles values and exemptions.

faqs.q: Can I run a short-term rental in a New Braunfels neighborhood?
faqs.a: Not in a residential zoning district, since the city's regulations bar short-term rentals there. Other districts generally need a special use permit and an annual fire inspection.

faqs.q: When do New Braunfels property taxes become delinquent?
faqs.a: They become delinquent on February 1, and a 6 percent penalty plus 1 percent interest are added that day under state law. The penalty rises to 12 percent by July 1.

faqs.q: Do I need to reapply for a homestead exemption after buying a house?
faqs.a: Yes, file Form 50-114 with the Comal Appraisal District, because the exemption belongs to the owner on January 1. A buyer who closes after that date can claim it for the rest of that tax year if the seller did not have one.
